queries.query: Design an AsyncAPI 3.0 specification for our "FreightPulse" logistics platform's event-driven architecture. We have three microservices — `shipment-tracker`, `warehouse-manager`, and `carrier-gateway` — communicating over Kafka and AMQP. The spec needs to cover these channels: `shipments/status-updated` (Kafka, carries shipment ID, GPS coordinates, timestamp, and status enum), `warehouse/inventory-reserved` (AMQP, includes order ID, SKU list with quantities, and warehouse code), and `carrier/rate-quoted` (Kafka, with carrier ID, lane info, rate breakdowns, and expiration time). Each message should use CloudEvents envelope format. I also need reusable schema components for shared types like `Address`, `GeoCoordinate`, and `MonetaryAmount`, proper server definitions for our dev/staging/prod Kafka clusters and RabbitMQ brokers, and operation bindings with appropriate Kafka consumer group IDs and AMQP exchange/routing key configs. We use Avro for Kafka messages and JSON for AMQP — please reflect that in the content types and schema formats accordingly. Also add security schemes for SASL/PLAIN on Kafka and username/password on AMQP, and include an `x-stability` extension on each channel so our tooling can flag breaking changes during CI.

queries.query: We receive nightly CSV feeds from 12 regional warehouses into `~/data/inventory_sync/` and before loading them into our Postgres warehouse I need a Python validation layer at `~/repos/inventory-pipeline/src/validators/`. Each CSV should conform to a JSON Schema I've drafted at `schemas/warehouse_feed_v3.json` (columns like `sku`, `quantity_on_hand`, `unit_cost`, `warehouse_code`, `last_counted_at`), but beyond structural validation I also need business rule checks: quantities can't be negative, unit costs must be between $0.01 and $50,000, `warehouse_code` must match one of our 12 known codes, `last_counted_at` can't be in the future or more than 90 days old, and no duplicate SKUs within a single warehouse file. On top of that, flag any statistical anomalies — if a SKU's `quantity_on_hand` deviates more than 3 standard deviations from its rolling 30-day average (historical stats are in a `sku_stats` table), mark it for manual review. Generate a per-file validation report as structured JSON summarizing total rows, rows passed, rows failed with reasons grouped by rule, and anomaly flags, and if any file has more than 5% failures, halt the load for that file and send an alert via our existing `alerts.send_slack_message()` helper. Can you build this out with good test coverage?
